Date: 2023-01-16 What is claimed is:
1. A medical-device system, comprising:
a risk stratification circuit configured to:
receive physiological information sensed from the patient;
generate distinct first, second, and third signal metrics using the received physiological information;
calculate a primary pulmonary risk score using the first pulmonary signal metric, and calculate a secondary pulmonary risk score using the second and the third pulmonary signal metrics;
calculate a composite pulmonary risk score using the primary and the secondary pulmonary risk scores; and
an output circuit configured to provide the calculated composite pulmonary risk to a user or a process.
2. The medical-device system of claim 1, comprising a physiological event detector circuit configured to automatically detect a cardiorespiratory event of the patient based at least in part on the calculated composite pulmonary risk score.
3. The medical-device system of claim 2, wherein to automatically detect the cardiorespiratory event, the physiological event detector circuit is configured to:
calculate a cardiorespiratory event score using one or more physiological signals sensed from the patient;
determine or adjust an alert threshold based at in part on the calculated composite pulmonary risk score; and
generate an alert of the cardiorespiratory event when the cardiorespiratory event score exceeds the alert threshold.
4. The medical-device system of claim 2, wherein the cardiorespiratory event includes at least one of worsening heart failure (WHF), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, or pulmonary edema.
5. The medical-device system of claim 1, wherein the first, the second, and the third signal metrics are each selected from the group consisting of:
a respiration rate;
a ratio of respiration rate to tidal volume;
a third heart sound (S3) intensity;
a ratio of the S3 intensity to a reference heart sound intensity;
a heart rate;
a thoracic impedance; and
a physical activity level.
6. The medical-device system of claim 1, wherein the risk stratification circuit is configured to calculate the secondary pulmonary risk score using measurements of the second signal metric obtained at times when the third signal metric satisfies a specified condition.
7. The medical-device system of claim 6, wherein the second signal metric include a respiratory rate and the third signal metric incudes a physical activity intensity or duration, wherein the measurements of the second signal metric include respiratory rates measured during a time period when the physical activity intensity or duration exceeds a threshold.
8. The medical-device system of claim 1, wherein the risk stratification circuit is configured to calculate the secondary pulmonary risk score using the second signal metric weighted by the third signal metric.
9. The medical-device system of claim 1, wherein the risk stratification circuit is configured to calculate the composite pulmonary risk score using a linear or a nonlinear combination of the primary and secondary pulmonary risk scores.
10. The medical-device system of claim 1, wherein the risk stratification circuit is configured to calculate the composite pulmonary risk score using a neural network taking the primary and the secondary pulmonary risk scores as input.
11. The medical-device system of claim 1, wherein the risk stratification circuit is configured to calculate the composite pulmonary risk score further using a classification of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) stages one through four.
12. The medical-device system of claim 1, comprising a therapy circuit configured to initiate or adjust a therapy to treat a cardiorespiratory disease in accordance with the calculated composite pulmonary risk score.
13. A method, comprising:
receiving physiological information sensed from the patient;
generating, via a risk stratification circuit of a medical-device system, distinct first, second, and third signal metrics using the received physiological information;
calculating, via the risk stratification circuit, a primary pulmonary risk score using the first pulmonary signal metric, and calculate a secondary pulmonary risk score using the second and the third pulmonary signal metrics;
calculating, via the risk stratification circuit, a composite pulmonary risk score using the primary and the secondary pulmonary risk scores; and
providing, via an output circuit, the calculated composite pulmonary risk to a user or a process.
14. The method of claim 13, further comprising automatically detecting a cardiorespiratory event of the patient based at least in part on the calculated composite pulmonary risk score, the cardiorespiratory event including at least one of worsening heart failure (WHF), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, or
pulmonary edema.
15. The method of claim 14, wherein automatically detecting the cardiorespiratory even includes:
calculating a cardiorespiratory event score using one or more physiological signals sensed from the patient;
determining or adjusting an alert threshold based at in part on the calculated composite pulmonary risk score; and
generating an alert of the cardiorespiratory event when the cardiorespiratory event score exceeds the alert threshold.
16. The method of claim 13, wherein calculating the secondary pulmonary risk score includes using measurements of the second signal metric obtained at times when the third signal metric satisfies a specified condition.
17. The method of claim 13, wherein calculating the secondary pulmonary risk score includes using the second signal metric weighted by the third signal metric.
18. The method of claim 13, wherein calculating the composite pulmonary risk score includes using a neural network taking the primary and the secondary pulmonary risk scores as input.
19. The method of claim 13, wherein calculating the composite pulmonary risk score further using a classification of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) stages one through four.
20. The method of claim 13, further comprising initiating or adjusting a therapy to treat a cardiorespiratory disease in accordance with the calculated composite pulmonary risk score. 40 41 42 43
